main_text.p: Interest profectò, maximè interest vestræ huius reipublicæ vt Romanæ illius feræ, quà fraude, qua violentia in omnes sinus terræ sibi auctoritatem potestatemque assumentis iniquitas in lucem quotidie magis magisque proferatur. Narrabant veteres quidam Pontum ita esse, vt omnes aquas in se recipiat, nullas emittat ex se: nam ibi esse gurgitem atque barathum vastissimum, quod veteres Græci [?]Βάραθρα πόντου appellabant. Romæ est Pontus, Romæ [?]βάθος, Romæ Pontum efficiens Pontifex, tendunt Omnia quem ver-sum vestigia, nulla retrorsum. Imperium o-lim ipso vlum est, ille abusus imperio: & ita abusus, vt centies illud Pontifex in suum Κάθος praecipitauerit, centies Deus ab illo exitio retraxerit; in quod tamen, proh dolor, paulatim non cessat ruere im-pellentibus & circumuenientibus retiariis Pontificis. Quid vestra hac repub. futu-rum esset, Deus bone, si illius technis ia-nua aliqua patefceret? Rimas conatur per suos emissarios, vt Ponto suo exundet in vos, vt in suum Κάθος hunc statum abripiat. Quo iure autem; facile hic visuri sunt o-mnes qui fidem ipsius in Rom. Imperii

page.notes: The Greek words in lines 11 and 12 are printed in a different, smaller type; my reading of them is doubtful. The text is cut off at the foot of this part and continues in part 2. The left margin contains only cropped show-through fragments; the Greek word "Κάθος" is printed as in the scan (Greek "Cάθος" as read, likely Κάθος / Κάθος). Some letters near the right edge are faint.
